work_packages.title: Freeze the public capability baseline and explicit simulation extensions
work_packages.target: One versioned configuration ledger says what aircraft is represented, what evidence supports each capability, which parameters are estimates, and which extensions are selected.

tasks.task: Create a public-baseline profile with an explicit dated evidence ledger; do not advertise a precise production block/software match without corresponding sources.

Use current ordinary land-based operation as the default intent, including documented later automatic backup oxygen behavior. A pre-ABOS manual-EOS representation is a separately dated historical option; modern reserve quantity remains an explicit estimate. No exact production block is asserted.

Record equipment capability, actual hardware fit, integration status and fleet fielding as separate attributes. A pod lua definition or a modernization contract does not establish an operational F-22 installation.
Create a Modernized simulation extension profile for complete optional optical targeting, HMD and other accepted additions; support mixing only through explicit per-capability compatibility rules.
Store evidence class, edition, page, source access, uncertainty, adopted analogue and parameter bounds next to each profile option. Fail unsupported combinations with a useful configuration message.

Pin a source/build/installed package/asset/default-input manifest and native capability profiles. Matching DLL copies do not prove build provenance or actual loaded identity; the sampled installed input defaults differ from the planning tree. Preserve saved user bindings and custom HUD/recordings during any deliberate migration.
Default to preserving supported functions and coherent existing policies; resolve uncertain details with configurable, bounded estimates instead of importing every Viper/Hornet feature.

normal: A saved profile deterministically loads the same equipment, controls, captions, backend requirements and procedures.
limit: A source describing development/testing is never relabeled universal fielding; unavailable classified detail remains an explicit uncertainty.
failure: A missing equipment backend produces a declared unsupported capability rather than silently enabling a panel-only imitation.
recovery: Loading another supported profile clears incompatible transient states and reports changed capabilities.

work_packages.evidence: F-22 functional public evidence + source-applicability policy; exact production configuration is a project decision.
work_packages.status: planned; implementation and runtime qualification remain separate

work_packages.title: Publish cross-system state and authority contracts
work_packages.target: Every shared quantity and action has one authoritative owner, units, validity, time basis and lifecycle; presentation never manufactures physical achievement.

tasks.task: Write a compact versioned contract for supplies/consumer availability; measured air data versus physics truth; navigation estimate versus true location; sensor observation versus receipt time; designated versus station-retained target; release intent versus native outcome; panel focus versus weapon-global commands; physical fault versus attention/audio.

For each migrated quantity record unit/reference, producer cadence, freshness, valid/degraded/unavailable states, permitted consumers and reset events. Keep existing parameter names behind temporary adapters until the owning vertical slice is qualified.
Correlate state-changing requests with request id, generation/mission epoch, result status and committed values. Readback equality alone is not an acknowledgement of a new request.
Separate real simulator observations, planned mission information and permitted debug truth. Do not make live tactical knowledge from unrestricted enemy-world queries.
Document which settings are shared by the physical sensor and which are local to each display. Do not move a physical sensor mode simply because another display opens its format.

Define multiplayer authority and replication per controlling aircraft/donor/server role: one physical release/mass owner, sender incarnation and sequence, compatible protocol version, duplicate/reordered-message behavior and join/reconnect reset. A remote SA report cannot become own-radar fire-control authority; replication of custom handles/draws requires actual host evidence.

Use explicit native readiness levels and reason codes: module/API bound, instance constructed, data valid, effect observed. Specify recoverable parameter-handle startup, coherent snapshot/commit and physics/model/render clock rules; do not collapse these into one READY boolean.

normal: Two consumers receive the same unit/reference/epoch and agree on authoritative achieved state.
limit: A stale valid flag cannot preserve an expired observation; zero remains a valid value when physically valid.
failure: Dropped, reordered, duplicated and rejected requests cannot yield a false success or revive old authority.
recovery: Producer restoration republishes a fresh epoch; consumers reconnect without replaying old commands.

work_packages.evidence: Implementation contract supporting source-backed behavior; exact software interfaces are mod design.
work_packages.status: planned; implementation and runtime qualification remain separate

work_packages.title: Define mission, power, pause, rearm and repair lifecycles
work_packages.target: A lifecycle matrix defines which physical, mission, pilot preference and temporary states survive each event.

tasks.task: Enumerate cold/hot/air spawn, mission restart, pause, time reversal, focus loss, power loss/restore, device loss, rearm, same-type reload, tank change, repair and aircraft destruction.
Give each pending entry, held input, station target, track, audio lease and native handle an epoch/cancellation owner. Distinguish structural repair from a whole-mission reset.
Release held actions to the owner that received their press; require a new deliberate press after power/focus restoration when appropriate.
Reconcile mass, station identity, fuel and backend readiness before dependent indications return to ready. Preserve documented preferences only according to an explicit memory policy.

For native adapters, declare allocation, hook/callback registration, outstanding-use quiescence, teardown and unsupported-build failure behavior. Keep diagnostic GPU/module lifetime effects distinct from ordinary service; require restart where a diagnostic pins process-lifetime state. Migrate one complete producer/consumer package with explicit rollback, never two physical owners simultaneously.

normal: Each supported spawn is internally consistent without simulated catch-up commands.
limit: A same-type replacement is identifiable even when a zero-inventory frame is never observed.
failure: Pause/focus/native teardown cannot strand PTT, slew, trigger, dispensing or a stale pending release.
recovery: Repair/rearm restores only the states listed in the matrix. Mission restart clears prior transient sensor lock, live designation, release consent, pending transactions and fault acknowledgement; restored preplanned missions come only from an explicitly selected validated mission/profile partition.

work_packages.evidence: Simulator integration requirements; not a claim about aircraft memory architecture.
work_packages.status: planned; implementation and runtime qualification remain separate

work_packages.title: Unify focus and held-input routing on every display
work_packages.target: Any relocated sensor format receives page-dependent HOTAS control only when focused, while intentional weapon-global/HUD ACM actions remain global.

tasks.task: Allocate command namespaces before extending controls. The captured keyboard light options10505–10512 are global and overlap an earlier EFM10500–10525 AFCS handler. Migrate the advertised light bindings/dispatch with compatibility notes and negative tests proving lights cannot engage/adjust AFCS. No saved profile activation or prior flight cause is inferred.
Replace final-owner SOI0/2 gates for page cursor axes with the common focused-format authority predicate; cover A-A and A-G paths separately.
Keep global GUN/SRM TMS/ACM exceptions explicit in the command table. Separate preview/corral from actual designation and execute only the intended transition.
Audit mouse, keyboard, joystick and axis event semantics as press/release, impulse or continuous. Preserve existing missing-release fixes and avoid synthesizing endless down commands.
Qualify the physical bezel labels, selected boxes and action ownership from the same control definition; log command/focus/target changes only when useful.

normal: Move radar to LMFD, RMFD, CMFD and PMFD, focus it, slew and designate in both roles.
limit: Focus a passive page while slew is held; the invisible radar stops responding without blocking deliberate global ACM commands. Exercise every advertised light command and assert AFCS state remains unchanged.
failure: Power/focus/page loss releases the original owner and cannot latch cursor, designate or trigger.
recovery: Reopen the format and deliberately press again; no old press or preview is committed.

work_packages.evidence: Named HOTAS analogue plus reproduced owner-gating difference AX11; exact F-22 switches undisclosed.
retain: Current shared bezel/controller and original-owner release routing

work_packages.title: Make numeric transactions acknowledge the committed setting
work_packages.target: Every edit has a truthful draft, validation result, correlated commit and achieved readback in matching units.

tasks.task: Correct heading readback conversion: F22_AP_HEADING is already degrees in the captured publication. Preserve circular heading comparison and magnetic/true reference handling.
Replace waypoint-ID-only acceptance with a request/commit sequence and accepted id/lat/lon/elevation values; never mark a dropped same-ID edit ENTERED.
Apply the sequence/status contract to stores, TACAN, ILS, course, altimeter and radio edits. Distinguish local validation error, owner rejection, pending, timeout and completion.

Retain same-option numeric submission as the declared mod policy; document clear-all, delete-digit, cancel and backout consistently. Hornet CLR second-press behavior is an optional substitute, not established F-22 hardware behavior.
Keep the ENTRY_FIELD-zero stores completion check and repeated-button/digit release fixes. Cancel drafts on authority/profile/station/power changes.

normal: Submit 0, 1, 90, 123 and 359 degree headings; each valid achieved setting acknowledges correctly. Commit a same-ID waypoint coordinate change and a stores quantity change.
limit: Enter the already-current value and confirm only after this request finishes; reject out-of-range and malformed values without changing the achieved state.
failure: Drop/delay/reorder a response or cancel while pending; no false ENTERED and no orphaned late application.
recovery: A fresh request after restoration succeeds and displays only its own status.

work_packages.evidence: Named DCS entry analogue + actual captured-Lua contract probes AX12/N10; interface policy is deliberate.
retain: Stores completion waits for ENTRY_FIELD zero
work_packages.status: planned; implementation and runtime qualification remain separate

work_packages.title: Prove and connect clear-voice radio backend
work_packages.target: Pilot selected radio, achieved tuning, receiving, transmitting and audio are connected to a qualified supported DCS voice backend.

tasks.task: Perform a bounded backend feasibility spike before building more radio UI. The captured registration has no complete active voice-radio path; NativeDatalink is a different role and is not proof of voice support.

Declare supported simulator build, radio instance count, bands/spacing/modulation, tune/readback API, receive/audio path and PTT capabilities. Use public supported interfaces first; isolate any version-sensitive adapter.
Implement separate radio power/availability, requested/achieved frequency, selected transmit radio, receiving and PTT states. COMMS MENU opens a menu; it is never the achieved transmit signal.
Connect explicit COM1/COM2 command bindings and confirm delivery with a controlled sender/receiver scenario. If a second receiver cannot work, show unavailable and keep the capability gap open.
Gate backend callbacks by lifecycle epoch and physical availability; do not report successful tuning when the backend failed.

normal: Tune a compatible sender, receive intelligible audio, select the intended transmitter and verify the counterpart receives only during deliberate PTT.
limit: Reject unsupported bands/spacing and prove radio-menu opening alone does not key the transmitter.
failure: Remove power or backend support; indications become unavailable and PTT releases.
recovery: Restore, retune if the chosen memory policy requires it, and deliberately transmit without old queued PTT.

work_packages.evidence: Public F-22 UHF/VHF role; dual-radio pilot workflow adopted from DCS Hornet/Viper. Exact F-22 tuning deck remains unknown.

work_packages.owner: Navigation/data model lead; root integration owner
work_packages.observable_target: Every indication and control consumer identifies quantity, units/reference, selected source, health/freshness, visibility and allowed coupling independently. Inspectable profile decisions precede code changes.

tasks.task: Write a producer/consumer table for attitude, heading, ground track, pressure altitude, geometric ASL/AGL, radar height, navigation position, LOC/GS, TACAN bearing/range, wind and clocks. Assign one owner per value.
Separate selection, availability, validity, alignment, uncertainty and drawing visibility. Publish explicit reason and time fields at native/Lua boundaries.
Freeze world-axis signs, radians/degrees, true/magnetic reference, distance/height units and pressure conversion. Station course variation is separate from ownship variation.
Publish the core and optional profile decisions ND01–ND16. Unknown equipment values get explicit simulation labels and limits.
Agree vehicle power/failure events and shared-source health. A numerical truth value alone cannot make a selected failed sensor healthy.
Agree command and UI ownership with root. UFC_Controller is the active physical path; older ICP_Flight_Pages logic is legacy unless deliberately routed.

normal_acceptance: Trace a healthy frame from pressure/GINS/radio input through HUD, UFD, NAV and AFCS; quantities, units and labels agree.
Toggle display true/magnetic reference without changing the stored physical path or selected physical heading.
limit_acceptance: Exercise north crossing, negative elevation, missing variation, time jumps and one invalid component among healthy peers.
A valid high radar measurement does not implicitly extend the RALT control range.
failure_acceptance: Invalidate one producer; consumers show the appropriate unavailable state instead of a valid zero.
Hiding the NAV format does not stop receiver updates, timing or route computation.
recovery_acceptance: Restore fresh source data. Selection/profile persists, while AP does not reengage without pilot intent.
retained_positives: True/world route math, independent receiver component flags and native pressure calculation already exist.
Keep mode selection distinct from preset editing.

tasks.action: Inventory every existing producer/consumer of engine, battery, APU, pressure, gear, brake, fuel, cabin and FCS states; document units, frame, timestamp, valid flag, authority and reset action.
Introduce a proposed EFM VehicleContext that holds immutable input/sensor snapshots, model states and one output snapshot. Start by wrapping existing formulas with no healthy-behavior retune.

Define causal update order: host inputs -> requests/faults -> available sources -> fuel/air/pressure demands -> achieved engine/actuator states -> forces/mass ledger -> exports. Resolve coupled feedback through bounded previous-step states/substeps, never competing Lua/EFM integration.
Declare cold/hot/air starts, repair, refuel, rearm, unlimited fuel, pause and teardown semantics separately. Preserve host-loaded fuel/loadout when callbacks arrive after initial reset.
Add a baseline replay fixture and machine-readable contract report. Record native host behaviors separately from pure-callback or stub evidence.

normal: Replay existing healthy hot/cold/air fixtures before and after extraction; same inputs produce the same achieved state and forces within numerical tolerances.
limit: Variable frame periods, repeated draw calls and large event bursts do not integrate physical motion twice; bounded substeps handle long physics dt.
failure: Missing/invalid producer yields invalid status and an intentional fallback; no false healthy zero and no source-state oscillation.
recovery: Two sequential missions, repair without restart, rearm without repair and GPU removal retain or clear only their declared states.

work_packages.title: Complete independent radio audio, preset and guard workflows
work_packages.target: Inspect, edit, confirm and tune are separate; audio/guard selection is truthful for each supported receiver.

tasks.task: Implement selected radio, inspected preset, edited preset and tuned channel as separate states. Adopt20 presets as an explicit interim simulation choice if backend supports it, not a documented F-22 count.
Use independently selected receiver volume/squelch and transmit source; browsing a preset does not retune until deliberate confirmation.
Implement main/guard monitoring only to the extent the backend actually receives both. Monitoring guard must not silently replace the main working frequency.
Document mode-dependent AM/FM/band and guard availability from the declared adapter capability. Keep unavailable controls disabled with an understandable reason.

normal: Inspect presetB while tunedA, confirmB, mute receiver1 while receiver2 remains audible, and monitor guard without losing the working channel.
limit: Empty/unsupported preset or modulation cannot replace a valid achieved setting.
failure: Delayed tune acknowledgement retains the truthful old tuned value while the new request is pending.
recovery: Cancel/retry and restore one receiver without changing the surviving receiver or replaying transmit intent.

work_packages.evidence: Viper preset-inspection behavior and Hornet independent radio/guard workflow are named substitutes.
work_packages.status: planned; implementation and runtime qualification remain separate

work_packages.title: Own fault identity, occurrence and master attention separately
work_packages.target: Acknowledgement affects attention, not the underlying condition; new fault occurrences remain identifiable while older conditions persist.

tasks.task: Replace aggregate-only caution acknowledgement with condition id, active/inactive, occurrence sequence, priority, onset, acknowledgement and recall state.
Give master attention one owner and leave individual fault indications active until their physical cause clears. Avoid competing draw-argument and forced-boolean owners.
Maintain an active list/recall/hidden-count contract even when terrain or another event wins the single forward message. Deduplicate repeat messages without losing distinct new causes.
Separate equipment validity from terrain/navigation validity. Define supported ground/phase inhibitions per alert family; actual F-22 inhibit matrix remains unknown.
Carry physical supply isolation into dependent loss-of-function alerts even if the original overtemperature clears. Integrate with vehicle-owned bleed/oxygen/cooling states.

normal: Acknowledge generator faultA; its individual condition remains. Add hydraulic faultB whileA persists and request new attention according to the adopted policy.
limit: Invalid navigation suppresses unavailable terrain guidance without automatically hiding a valid equipment condition.
failure: Several active conditions retain identities when one urgent event owns attention; missing producer validity is shown explicitly.
recovery: Clear each physical cause independently; a recurrence receives a new occurrence rather than inheriting old acknowledgement.

work_packages.evidence: Hornet master-attention analogue and general crew-interface policy. Exact F-22 inhibit/acknowledgement matrix is not known; CG02/03/04 remain qualified design targets.
work_packages.status: planned; implementation and runtime qualification remain separate
integration_exit_gates: VEH-04/05/06/11/12/14: provider-owned condition identity, validity, isolation and recovery; framework can be implemented earlier.

tasks.task: Retain bare-STT nonresponse as no new hostile evidence. Mark complete native class values as simulator-assisted unless a declared game authentication/recognition event supplies the evidence.
Add ambiguous/conflict presentation and evidence inspection with per-source age; maintain a separate friendly-protection policy instead of hiding contradictory evidence.
Implement an abstract ownship responder state, incoming-reply indication and optional emergency-identification control through qualified host capabilities or explicitly labeled game events.
Keep interrogation AUTO/SCAN/LOS requests separate from transponder state, PPLI and radar power; define surviving CNI behavior through the common supply/resource contract.
Treat NCTR/Mode5 menus or detailed key controls as selected abstraction/research, with no real cryptography or copied Hornet recognition limits claimed as F-22 data.

normal: Positive native friendly identity is distinct from no-positive reply; retained earlier classification is visibly identity memory.
Independent ownship responder availability/replies can be observed without issuing a contact interrogation.
limit: No reply alone does not declare hostile; conflicting qualified sources become visibly ambiguous.
PPLI transmission is not displayed as proof of a transponder reply.
failure: Expired identity and failed responder capability yield unknown/unavailable rather than invented authentication.
recovery: Supply/resource restoration follows the declared identification state and does not replay old requests.

tasks.action: Implement a single SI calculation layer that exposes CAS/EAS/TAS/Mach/static/impact pressure and validity; migrate each threshold explicitly instead of changing every EAS gate to CAS by search/replace.

Instrument level, banked, inverted and ballistic host callbacks to resolve whether body ay includes gravity. Set one documented signed-Nz convention for limiter and presentation; do not subtract/add 1 merely from a generic sensor article.
Keep body and world wind transforms consistent; run airborne uniform wind/ground-velocity translation invariance at fixed achieved configuration with ground logic disabled.
Introduce sensor channel states for invalid, frozen and biased inputs without changing true airflow. Feed measured health to selected control reversion and indicate which datum is degraded.

Characterize native probe heat, ice/rain and weather interfaces. Implement a named estimated heater/test and sensor-degradation abstraction only for effects not already provided; separate sensor freezing from actual ice lift/drag effects.

normal: Analytic pitot samples from subsonic through supersonic conditions agree across HUD, AFCS and code; declared configuration gates use the same named quantity.
limit: Invalid pressure, speed-of-sound and nonfinite data invalidate the relevant channel; wind-translation invariance applies only airborne at fixed configuration.
failure: Frozen probe/sensor data changes indications/control availability while force generation continues to use true air state; no double icing effect.
recovery: Heater/source restoration changes sensor state using labelled estimated recovery, with stable transfer to normal control and no hidden trim impulse.

normal: Open takeoff and landing references and a selected active fault’s related page with a clear return path.
limit: Missing weight/trim/source displays unavailable and cannot mark an item complete.
failure: A higher-priority event gains attention without destroying the pilot’s selected reference or active fault list.

work_packages.title: Qualify voice arbitration, priority and retained mute policy
work_packages.target: Attention priority, actual playback, muting and audio-test status are separate, bounded states.

tasks.task: Specify a provisional mod latency budget for urgent warnings across an occupied voice slot; implement preemption or bounded completion based on measured clip lengths and adopted policy, without claiming recovered F-22 timing.
Retain confirmed-playback accounting and bounded leases. Mark speech delivered only when actual playback is confirmed; prevent failed/stale audio sources from blocking all later alerts.

Make the IR seeker audio consumer honor expiring MWS/pilot-audio authority rather than raw priority alone. Normalize native boolean and numeric0/1 is_playing returns in IR_Audio consistently with Warning_Audio_Gate; qualify actual host return forms and audible recovery in a controlled trial.

Preserve the deliberate global pilot-voice inhibit option: Viper documents all-voice mute. Consider a retained forward-field mute reminder as an optional usability policy, not a mandatory real F-22 feature.
Define arbitration with RWR/MWS tones, radio/intercom and test speech. Real urgent conditions cancel tests; do not queue obsolete terrain commands after the threat changes.
Calibrate volume/mute independently of HUD text and fault state. Keep voice-test naming scoped to recordings, distinct from lamp/equipment BIT.

normal: An urgent active event obtains its declared audio/visual response while ordinary speech or test occupies the slot.
limit: All-voice inhibit behaves consistently; audio display reports retained state and zero volume does not erase active alerts.
failure: Missing clip, failed host status or an endlessly true playing flag cannot create a permanent mute.
recovery: Restore audio and announce only still-relevant events under the repetition policy; no replay of expired commands.

# Sensor peer review of the cross-system plan

Reviewed `work/overhaul/root.json` against `sensors.json` and the unchanged 2026-10-27 12:58:25 MDT capture. No aircraft/output edits. The optional mission-data, boom-versus-probe and alert-policy evidence boundaries are appropriately qualified; no additional real F-22 procedure or performance overclaim was found.

## Concrete wording corrections

1. **ARC-03 recovery: distinguish transient target state from deliberately reloaded mission data.** “Mission restart never retains a prior mission target” is broader than SEN-09/MIS-01’s intended PP mission retention/import policy. Use: “Mission restart never retains prior transient sensor lock, live designation, release consent or pending transaction; any restored PP mission comes from an explicitly selected validated mission/profile partition.” The distinction is supported by the existing separate captured-station and live-program snapshots (`AG_Stores.lua:54–56,63–69`) and the named Hornet per-station PP/TOO distinction (ED guide p332). Neither source establishes real F-22 mission-restart persistence; this remains a mod policy.

2. **AUX-01: explicitly retain the existing fuel callback and mass accounting.** The captured `RAPTOR.cpp:1583–1587` already reports tanker acceptance from available internal/external capacity. `1593–1619` accepts incremental kilograms, fills internal then host-reported external tanks and queues the mass changes. Add these to `retain`, and frame the missing work as qualifying door/readiness/contact/disconnect and host integration, not creating a previously absent fuel-transfer model. The acceptance callback presently checks capacity, not achieved receptacle state; whether another host path provides that interlock is unverified. Keep the proposed source/EDM investigation before adding or duplicating a fuel/door gate.

## Cross-lane edges to make explicit in the assembled plan

3. **One equipment and availability ledger.** Make ARC-01 the authoritative equipment/profile schema, with SEN-01 supplying its sensor/store evidence and feasibility entries rather than creating a competing profile loader. ARC-02 should own the common consumer-availability contract; CNI-03, SEN-02, SEN-05, SEN-07 and SEN-08 consume/publish their own qualified resource states. A generic CNI resource budget must not silently become a documented common radar/EW failure topology. Brower pp9/11 supports reconfiguration roles, not the proposed exact resource capacities or priorities.

4. **MIS-01 → SEN-05/SEN-06; optional PP import → SEN-09.** Give planned rings, pilot declarations, network defaults and imported PP coordinates separate source types. Importing a planned hostile label must not create a measured radar contact, an authenticated IFF result or weapon-support authority; an imported coordinate mission follows the deliberate station-assignment/ACK path. Preserve the current native-peer restriction to onboard radar reports (`NativeDatalink.cpp:294–313`) so mission overlays cannot leak into live-track transmission. These are dependencies of the optional importer on core contracts, not reasons to block the core sensor packages on a map/DTC implementation.

5. **ALR-02 ↔ SEN-07/SEN-08/SEN-10 and CNI-02.** Include IR seeker tones and any new CM consent/start/completion speech in the arbitration contract. This is an existing coupling: `Weapon_System.lua:632–635` directly inhibits `IR_Audio` using MWS/pilot priority; `IR_Audio.lua:5–7` immediately suppresses levels. A new central arbiter must preserve or intentionally replace that path. Define separately pilot-voice inhibit, warning/seeker tone policy, receiver volume and radio PTT; the Viper all-voice-inhibit example does not establish an all-audio mute or a real F-22 priority order.

6. **UI-01/UI-03 ↔ SEN-03/SEN-04/SEN-12/SEN-14.** Distinguish a panel-local inspection cursor/range/declutter from the physical sensor’s commanded cursor, scale and mode. A deliberate focused sensor command may intentionally change shared sensing and should update every duplicate view; merely opening or zooming a local view must not. Current `Radar_Computer` has one sensor cursor/selection, while `Sensor_Control` determines focused-format authority. Apply that same contract before adding pod/HMD controls, preserving the weapon-global ACM exception.

7. **ARC-03/AUX-01 ↔ vehicle fuel/station lifecycle and SEN-09.** Reconcile refueling, tank changes, jettison, reload and repair through the same physical station-generation/mass owner. Do not infer a new weapon generation from fuel quantity, or a delivered shot from a jettison/service decrement. SEN-09-T04/T05 correctness work can start after the shared contract is agreed; it need not wait for optional mission-data, pod or HMD completion.

These edges clarify integration ownership and acceptance scope; they do not add aircraft-specific operational algorithms or undocumented F-22 controls.

# Vehicle review of the root overhaul plan

Reviewed `work/overhaul/root.json` against `work/overhaul/vehicle.json` and the unchanged 2026-10-27 12:58:25 MDT source capture. No JSON or aircraft source was changed. This review concerns cross-lane implementation ownership and prerequisites; it does not reopen the aircraft-comparison grades.

## Required corrections before assembly

1. **Make modern ABOS part of the chosen ordinary-operation baseline, rather than an unresolved later option.** ARC-01 task 2 currently says, “Keep a historical pre-ABOS option separate from a later ABOS choice.” This leaves the ordinary baseline ambiguous relative to VEH-12 and VD01, which select automatic backup. Replace with: “The ordinary-operation public baseline includes the documented later automatic backup oxygen behavior. A pre-ABOS manual-EOS representation is a separately dated historical option; exact modern reserve capacity remains an explicit simulation estimate/decision.” Cite the [2013 Edwards installation article](https://www.edwards.af.mil/News/Article/394043/edwards-airmen-vital-to-raptors-return/) / VS06. The [2012 SAB report](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/PDF/DocumentFile/Documents/2012/AFSAB_Oxygen_020112.pdf) / VS05 is pre-ABOS architecture evidence and must not supply the default manual procedure or modern backup endurance. This does not assert an exact modern aircraft block.

2. **CNI-03 must consume the vehicle supply/cooling contract, not introduce another electrical or thermal owner.** Its file list includes `Electrical_Computer.lua` and `Navigation_Power.lua` but no explicit vehicle provider prerequisite. VEH-04 migrates physical supply integration to the EFM; VEH-11 owns reduced-order cooling. Amend CNI-03 to define *consumer resource allocation and recovery* only, with provider availability/health inputs from VEH-04/VEH-11. `Electrical_Computer.lua` may remain a temporary compatibility adapter; CNI must not add SOC, voltage, generator or thermal integration there.

   A specific existing bridge also needs an integration task: `EFM/source/NativeNavigation.cpp:263` connects native ILS DC/AC feeds; lines 267–270 derive `on` from aggregate `MAIN_POWER` and drive both native generator interfaces with it. A new essential/emergency CNI policy cannot work simply by leaving that all-or-nothing gate unchanged. Map declared radio/navigation consumer feeds to supported native buses or a truthful degraded/unavailable state. Keep *actual generator source state*, *consumer availability* and *native bus bridge enable* distinct; do not relabel an aggregate bridge enable as two healthy physical generators. The three-line `Navigation_Power.lua` contains no physical reserve model to extend.

3. **AUX-01 needs the fuel, power and FCS providers as named integration dependencies.** ARC-02/03 alone do not establish actual fuel delivery or source availability. Add VEH-03 for tank identity/contents/capacity/mass transactions; VEH-04 for the chosen physical supply interface; VEH-07 for selected refueling configuration and its control-law/speed-brake consequences. Hydraulic routing through VEH-06 should be an explicit *conditional interface dependency* after the receptacle actuator’s actual source is chosen, rather than assuming Hornet-style plumbing. The [1998 F-22 development paper](https://man.fas.org/dod-101/sys/ac/docs/f-22-emd-paper.htm) documents a separate AR configuration, but does not prove the production mode entry is identical to “door requested open.”

   The actual fuel callback/ledger belongs to VEH-03. AUX-01 should own the request/achieved door/contact/transfer/disconnect adapter and call that provider; it must not integrate a second fuel quantity or mass delta. Current capacity acceptance is at `RAPTOR.cpp:1583–1587`, and actual incremental transfer/mass changes are at `1593–1619`. `Electrical_System.lua:154` copies external argument 22 into AAR_READY; that copy must not become assumed physical contact without the planned mapping test.

4. **AUX-02 needs VEH-04 before its supply-loss acceptance can be completed.** The file name `Electrical_System.lua` is misleading: it currently handles AAR/light requests and knobs, not the physical electrical model. Preserve that role. The actual Boolean reduction exists at `RAPTOR.cpp:2145` / `2152`; draw exports then emit binary values, including line 1465. AUX-02 owns knob/enable/intensity/material mapping, while VEH-04 owns supply availability and load accounting. Add emitter/consumer IDs and a power-demand handoff so continuous intensity does not create an independent supply owner. Actual EDM/native emitter support remains a characterization gate, as already written.

5. **Alert integration needs explicit provider gates, not just ARC-02/03.** The ALR-01 framework can be implemented early, but its final fault-list/clear/recurrence acceptance must consume vehicle-owned fault identity, active state and validity from the actual providers. Add named integration edges from VEH-04, VEH-05, VEH-06, VEH-11, VEH-12 and VEH-14. ALR-02 needs the chosen alert/audio consumer supply from VEH-04 and the CNI audio contract from CNI-01/02 for its radio/intercom arbitration acceptance. ALR-03 needs VEH-02 for measured air-data health and VEH-07/09 for achieved configuration before claiming configuration-bound limit cues. These may be *integration exit gates*, rather than forcing the early generic alert framework to wait for every physical implementation.

   Current warning command acceptance and runtime power gating use `MAIN_POWER` (`Pilot_Warning_System.lua:137` and `274`), while VEH-04 will establish per-consumer availability. Decide and publish the selected simulation alert/audio feed; do not retain an accidental aggregate gate that contradicts the new load-shedding model. No exact F-22 essential-bus routing is inferred by this recommendation. Acknowledgment remains an alert action, never a repair or source restoration.

6. **Resolve @case package aliases exactly, and preserve the distinction between implementation and host qualification.** The intended root assignments are correct if the assembler resolves them to the vehicle packages below. Do not leave the alias as a dangling implementation owner or convert VT03’s decision gate into an unsupported claim that a wholly new canopy model is mandatory.

## Proposed cross-lane dependency edges

In this table, `A → B` means A supplies a prerequisite to B. “Exit gate” lets generic framework work proceed before the provider is complete; the integrated capability cannot claim completion until the contract is demonstrated.

| Prerequisite → dependent | Kind | Concrete handoff |
|---|---|---|
| ARC-01/ARC-02 → VEH-01 | Contract | Global profile/evidence/authority conventions constrain the vehicle state contract. |
| ARC-03 ↔ VEH-01 | Collaborative contract, not two hard graph edges | ARC-03 owns the whole-mod lifecycle matrix; VEH-01 supplies the physical-state rows. Publish one matrix and use a single graph direction for implementation ordering to avoid a cycle. |
| VEH-03 → AUX-01 | Hard integration dependency | Tank identity, accepted fuel increment, overflow, feed policy and one host mass ledger. |
| VEH-04 → AUX-01 | Hard integration dependency | Chosen actuator/control/indication consumer availability. |
| VEH-07 → AUX-01 | Exit gate | Request versus achieved refueling configuration, shared FCS mode/cue contract; no inferred door-only production mode entry. |
| VEH-06 → AUX-01 | Conditional | Only the source-limited hydraulic/pneumatic actuator route that is actually selected. |
| VEH-04 → AUX-02 | Hard integration dependency | Actual lamp feed/load and achieved emission availability; knob preference remains separate. |
| VEH-04/VEH-11 → CNI-03 | Hard integration dependency | Physical feeds, cooling health and capacity; CNI allocation cannot generate electrical energy or cool equipment. |
| CNI-01 → VEH-04 load-table completion | Contract/exit gate | Supported native receiver/transmitter instances and their declared simulated load/eligibility; not a reverse hard dependency for the basic power-model implementation. |
| VEH-04/05/06/11/12/14 → ALR-01 integration | Exit gate | Physical condition ID, active/cleared/degraded state and validity, distinct from acknowledgment/recall. |
| VEH-04 + CNI-01/02 → ALR-02 integration | Exit gate | Alert/audio feed and radio/intercom playback arbitration. |
| VEH-02/07/09 → ALR-03 integration | Exit gate | Measured air data and achieved FCS/gear configuration for cue eligibility; warning thresholds remain source-bound estimates. |
| VEH-04/07/09/11/12/14 → UI-04 content | Exit gate | Actual modeled procedures and fault actions; no copy of obsolete EMD workarounds or pre-ABOS manual-EOS procedure into the modern default. |
| VEH-14 + VEH-07 → UI-03 FCS presentation | Exit gate | Actual damaged/saturated achieved effectors and persistent versus resettable faults (P16). |
| VEH-11 → UI-03 cabin presentation | Exit gate | Pressure/reference/validity contract (P17). |
| ARC-03 + VEH-13 → REL-01 escape/lifecycle slice | Exit gate | Native escape result and subsequent aircraft/mission reset; no invented real seat limits. |
| VEH-15 → REL-01 final vehicle qualification | Hard release gate | Source/build/configuration-tagged normal, limit, degraded and recovery evidence, including performance conditions and resource conservation. |

These edges should be added to the combined plan’s cross-lane graph, not blindly inserted as mutual whole-package dependencies. VEH-03’s core ledger precedes its later hydraulic boost feedback; similarly CNI backend capability can inform the vehicle load table while the basic power model proceeds independently.

## Public baseline and optional-extension consistency

- **Retain as ordinary baseline targets:** finite fuel and power, documented SES/self-start functional roles, ground APU services, hydraulic and brake-source behavior, conditioned-air/cooling/cabin functions, and documented later automatic oxygen backup. Missing implementation is a work item; it does not make a documented aircraft function an optional modernization.
- **Keep explicitly estimated within that baseline:** source-limited cell allocation/transfer rates; detailed bus/routing and load capacities; thermal curves/cabin schedule; modern ABOS reserve quantity; production approach/control schedules and nozzle actuator mapping. The Eaton F119 “fueldraulics” description does not settle every nozzle feed, and the current per-side aircraft-hydraulic TVC mapping remains provisional.
- **Keep historical evidence scoped:** the 1998 paper’s configuration/mixing and approach examples are useful best-known targets but not a recovered modern OFP; rejected cooling handshakes, brake deadbands and temporary procedures are excluded. The 2012 OBOGS report does not override the later ABOS evidence. The historical cold-weather preheat statement does not impose a universal wait.
- **Keep separate optional additions:** unsourced automatic landing, particular modern HMD/optical targeting hardware fits and other modernization extensions. No vehicle package requires carrier launch/recovery hardware or imported Hornet flap/G/parking/anti-skid numbers.

The root’s general DEC-BASELINE and scope warnings agree with the vehicle plan once ARC-01 makes the ABOS default explicit and the provider/consumer boundaries above are connected.

decisions.recommendation: Native-host feasibility is a release gate. If absent, show unavailable or explicitly sensor-only functionality.
decisions.reason: Do not invent weapon guidance or fictional success states to fill a missing integration path.

decisions.chosen_default: Use one public-source F-22 simulation profile with modern automatic oxygen backup; retain source-era tags per feature. Do not claim a fully recovered current production block.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Record the modeled source-era choices in the aircraft manual and source ledger.
decisions.source_limit: A 1998 control behavior and 2014 component brochure do not establish one exact contemporary OFP.

decisions.chosen_default: EFM integrates physical quantities; Lua emits requests and renders derived outputs. Migrate one model at a time while retaining public parameter names.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Golden replay before/after each owner cutover.
decisions.source_limit: An architectural choice, not a statement about the real aircraft IVSC design.

decisions.chosen_default: Use explicit quantity names. Keep existing gate behavior until its intended physical meaning is selected; then migrate gate and documentation together.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Analytic compressible pitot grid and threshold/altitude comparisons.
decisions.source_limit: No public F-22 calibration/position-error table available.

decisions.chosen_default: Keep the current formula pending the narrowly specified host experiment; mark the signal unqualified rather than correcting it from generic physics alone.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Level/banked/inverted/ballistic callback traces.
decisions.source_limit: SDK semantics in captured comments do not settle gravity inclusion.

decisions.chosen_default: Retain 8,200 kg aggregate. Make cell distribution/locations configurable and explicitly estimated until sourced.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Public geometry/model geometry constraints and conservation sensitivity.
decisions.source_limit: Do not adopt inconsistent rescue-table quantities.

decisions.chosen_default: Retain mod VLO tank capacity provenance and callback-reported station IDs; retain 25 kg unusable fuel only as a labelled temporary estimate.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Host empty-attached versus removed tank test and feed-starvation calibration.
decisions.source_limit: Mod tank artwork/definition is not production F-22 tank certification.

decisions.chosen_default: Implement role/topology interfaces first; require a checked configuration table before enabling per-cell shortages. No invented production cell split is selected in this plan.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Public diagram/geometry-supported estimates plus sensitivity report.
decisions.source_limit: A missing exact split does not justify copying F-16 reservoirs.

decisions.chosen_default: Retain existing 12 Ah, 18 A, 80 A start increment and 8 A charge as initial simulation parameters while introducing actual consumer loads.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Load audit and source-loss endurance replay.
decisions.source_limit: Public 28 V battery evidence does not authenticate capacity or current draws.

decisions.chosen_default: Adopt continuous both-generator/both-engine qualification for 60 seconds as initial compatibility policy; document it as DCS-inspired.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: F-22-specific source could supersede policy; test interrupted qualification.
decisions.source_limit: One-minute second-generator rule is Hornet documentation, not F-22 proof.

decisions.chosen_default: Use finite normalized reservoirs with explicit servicing; numeric capacity and cold-soak thresholds are release calibration inputs. Do not force a temperature-independent universal wait.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Capacity evidence if public, otherwise clearly labelled normalized-budget tuning and sensitivity.
decisions.source_limit: Historical shelter preheat statement does not establish a current control schedule.

decisions.chosen_default: Retain current finite lag/ramp values as first regression baseline, then tune linked combustion and instruments with declared simulated envelopes.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Throttle/start/relight/abort traces over atmosphere and source conditions.
decisions.source_limit: No matched F119 transient/temperature/oil deck is available.

decisions.chosen_default: Maintain separate total consumed fuel and main-burner/augmentation quantities; choose displayed quantity explicitly per cockpit equipment evidence.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Public F-22 display documentation; temporary display choice labelled if unresolved.
decisions.source_limit: Hornet IFEI excluding AB flow does not establish F-22 indication semantics.

decisions.chosen_default: Preserve current independent achieved TVC and vector mechanics, but treat left/right aircraft-hydraulic feed as provisional. Add an engine-actuation interface before final mapping.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Reconcile public Eaton F119 fueldraulics statement with any available nozzle actuator schematic/function evidence.
decisions.source_limit: Brochure does not uniquely identify every nozzle actuator feed.

decisions.chosen_default: Retain 3,950 psi display/consumer reference until its measurement point is defined; separately encode published component ratings in the source table.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Define regulation, line losses and displayed transducer location; calibrate no-load/demand response.
decisions.source_limit: 4,100 psi pump rating alone cannot falsify every 3,950 psi consumer value.

decisions.chosen_default: Use documented normal utility/maintenance distinction and rudder alternative feed; all additional routing stays explicitly estimated.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Public complete schematic if available; otherwise route-by-function failure tests and sensitivity.
decisions.source_limit: No automatic left/right equivalence or claim that the brochure excludes every backup path.

decisions.chosen_default: Use historical 12-degree normal / 11.5-degree selected single-engine reference and 35/20-degree flap examples only in a labelled public best-known configuration, pending production evidence.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Normal/one-engine approach handling, cue and selected-mode consistency.
decisions.source_limit: 1998 EMD values are a historical anchor, not today’s certified schedule.

decisions.chosen_default: Retain absolute 20-degree pitch travel. Keep Mach/WOW/rate schedules as estimates and calibrate them separately.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Achieved-angle/force/animation and failed-source traces.
decisions.source_limit: Manufacturer maximum does not mean full travel at every condition.

decisions.chosen_default: Use stabilization/protection pitch demand first, then roll within remaining bounded authority as an initial tunable policy.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Combined-demand maneuver/recovery response and saturation trace.
decisions.source_limit: Not claimed as proprietary F-22 allocation logic.

decisions.chosen_default: Retain pitch 0.04 and lateral 0.02 normalized units/s with 0.25-second pitch release settling until handling evidence supports change.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Preserve frame/event-rate invariance and measured approach handoff.
decisions.source_limit: These are current mod tuning, not F-22 trim actuator rates.

decisions.chosen_default: Retain existing deck as a versioned baseline and mark unsupported cells; change through matched-condition force/energy/fuel calibration rather than claiming a published deck.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Joint dry/AB, level-flight/climb/acceleration/turn/approach/fuel grid.
decisions.source_limit: 35,000-lb thrust class and supercruise headline do not determine exact installed curves.

decisions.topic: Mass inertia, stores drag and ground effect
decisions.chosen_default: Host experiment selects one owner for each effect. Add only demonstrated missing contributions.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Point-mass movement, empty/full external stores and fixed-height sweeps with identical achieved configuration.
decisions.source_limit: Zero MOI transaction or no literal ground-effect term is not proof of absent total host behavior.

decisions.chosen_default: Use a continuous bounded estimated steering schedule and consistent WOW/command guard; existing 60/25-degree and speed thresholds are tuning baselines, not public F-22 limits.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Taxi/takeoff/landing and contact-bounce traces; code versus binding equivalence.
decisions.source_limit: No copied Hornet launch bar/free-fall command or certified F-22 gear speed claim.

decisions.chosen_default: Keep native wheel anti-skid initially while measuring it; add one aircraft-level deceleration controller only through a supported interface. Parking state must be idempotent and pressure-qualified.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Wheel/slip/deceleration and ground-friction tests; document controller responsibility.
decisions.source_limit: Do not copy historical faulty deadband or unresolved Viper parking-release RPM.

decisions.chosen_default: Separate finite stored fluid from brake energy/heat soak. Numeric volumes, heat capacity, cooling and fade remain labelled calibration inputs.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Conservation and repeated-stop/cooling sensitivity; host thermal ownership first.
decisions.source_limit: Rescue waiting instructions are not a thermal response curve.

decisions.chosen_default: Implement ambient plus separate bounded increment with seal/leak dynamics; leave exact modern schedule as a named estimate.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: SDK export convention plus pressure-altitude consistency and source-loss scenarios.
decisions.source_limit: SAB upstream 35 psi and OBOGS pressure are not cabin pressure.

decisions.chosen_default: Choose a reduced air/fuel/coolant heat network; qualitative dependencies first, identified estimated time constants and load capacities next.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Source-loss/heat-load/fuel/ram-air/fog sensitivity.
decisions.source_limit: Do not reproduce rejected EMD defects or conflate tint with fog removal.

decisions.chosen_default: Use Pa; retain healthy export baseline until pressure-reference/host-response experiment. Keep concentration, cabin pressure and delivery state separate.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Controlled host interface experiment; no clinical extrapolation.
decisions.source_limit: SDK establishes pressure unit, not mask partial pressure or host physiology.

decisions.chosen_default: Modern automatic transfer is required by public evidence; finite reserve quantity is configurable and must be labelled estimated if exact data remain unavailable. No old EOS duration is adopted.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Inventory/source-transition tests and explicit profile capacity decision before release.
decisions.source_limit: 2012 manual EOS endurance cannot be modern ABOS capacity.

decisions.chosen_default: Prefer native adapter if motion/hold/lock/power states can be observed and controlled; otherwise replace the competing writer once.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Native canopy state observation.
decisions.source_limit: Input inheritance makes absence in an owned Lua file inconclusive.

decisions.chosen_default: Repair restores supported health and clears matching faults; start, refuel, recharge, rearm and cooling remain separate servicing actions unless explicitly included.
decisions.calibration_or_evidence_needed: Sequential failure/repair/service/respawn scenario table.
decisions.source_limit: No new assertion that the already-fixed derived-integrity repair bug persists.

coordinated_reviews.text:
# F-22 overhaul acceptance campaign

Prepared 27 October 2026. Read-only planning result; no aircraft, mission, installed mod, canonical audit or DCS process was changed. **Every execution result in this campaign is NOT RUN.** Source inspection, extracted reference pages and two rendered reference pages are the evidence produced here. They are not simulator qualification.

The campaign complements the system workstreams by testing complete pilot tasks and transitions. A display selection, successful Lua test, C++ callback, initialized readiness parameter or attractive preview cannot close a flight or native-GPU acceptance item.

## 1. Configuration and evidence contract

### Dated test fixture and project release profile

**ARC-01 owns the single project-wide public-baseline capability/evidence ledger and separate Modernized simulation options.** Its adopted release profile controls WP00 and the mandatory gates. This document proposes **B2014 solely as a dated TEST FIXTURE**: a selected Increment 3.1 and ABOS-equipped, land-based F-22A reference configuration dated 10 April 2014. It is not a competing project baseline or an exact OFP assertion. Every card is parameterized by ARC-01's equipment sheet. B2014 does not assert that every aircraft had that configuration on that date. Record individual capability selections; do not invent a Block/OFP identifier. [R1, R2, R3]

The fixture samples the conventional internal A/A fit, gun, two-internal-GBU-32 A/G fit, Increment 3.1 surface mapping/designation, and installed automatic backup oxygen. It does **not** exhaust the capabilities of Increment 3.1: operational GBU-39 SDB employment is explicitly documented in 2012. ### Initial engineering budgets

These are proposed **MOD-P** acceptance thresholds for WP00/discipline owners to freeze before execution. They must not be advertised as real-aircraft limits or adjusted after a failed run without a recorded rationale and rerun.

* UI input: one press yields exactly one action; release reaches the original owner even after a page/focus change. No release/fire/dispense resumes after power restoration without the declared fresh-consent action. Input quench is observed within 0.10 s or two measured owner update periods, whichever is greater.
* Numeric entry: invalid/out-of-range text does not change the achieved value; a positive acknowledgement requires readback. The current UFC pending timeout is 1 s; allow one measured UI update for observing the timeout message (S11).
* Basic instrument crosscheck: for stable data with common units/reference, HUD/ADI/telemetry agree within display quantization plus 1 kt, 10 ft and 0.5 degree. Do not apply this between CAS/EAS/TAS, radar/barometric altitude, or true/magnetic headings without conversion.
* AFCS performance: after 15 s settling, hold for 60 s with altitude error <=100 ft and heading/attitude error <=2 degrees in the nominal fixture; no growing oscillation or hidden pilot assistance. Coupled-route cross-track error <=0.2 NM on a straight leg after capture. A declared commanded turn has a separate transient budget. Engagement/disconnect predicates must match the adopted contract exactly.
* Fuel/mass: reconcile start + added - burned - leaked - jettisoned - end quantities. Residual <= max(1 kg, 0.1% of start fuel) over an instrumented five-minute segment, and no unexplained mass step. Separately prove the host mass-change callback and store mass ledger. Round displayed pounds only after comparing SI ledgers.
* Image registration: two independently surveyed scene landmarks at different screen locations agree with the displayed/designated coordinates within 2% of active image width in a nominal static case. Moving-case temporal registration error must fit the measured source refresh interval plus 0.10 s and never use a future pose. A capability owner must freeze a stricter targeting budget before guided-delivery fidelity closure; passing this image test alone does not prove SAR or weapon accuracy.
* Alert lifecycle: no urgent event is silently dropped. Proposed urgent audible/visual onset <=0.5 s from a valid producer condition, with the producer delay and audio scheduling delay measured separately. Any intentional source-specific delay must be separately declared; do not replace historical F-22 sensing delays with this generic presentation budget.
* Regression stability: repeat identical deterministic nominal cases three times; no unexplained count/state differences. Where physics is noisy, report mean/range and the predeclared tolerance, not a blanket bit-for-bit requirement.

Use two independent outcomes: **functional result** PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT RUN/N/A and **fidelity status** F22-D/ANALOGUE/MOD-P/UNKNOWN. N/A requires a documented configuration exclusion. PARTIAL can describe evidence coverage but does not satisfy a release gate. Failures preserve first evidence and exact reproduction steps; reruns do not erase them.

### M12 - Optional Black Glass capstone and regression (about 20-30 min; all applicable earlier gates required)

N/A exclusions and BLOCKED items are visible. |

**Profile-sensitive gates:** G0 uses ARC-01's authoritative release ledger, not B2014 as a project baseline. Selecting different weapon generations/equipment changes G4/M06-M07 and G5/M08-M09/SDB requirements. Selecting EOS versus ABOS changes G6/M10's oxygen response. Selecting a different documented display/CNI/AFCS capability changes the applicable G2/G3/M02-M04 tasks. VR/MP claims activate the relevant G7 hardware/deployment cases; Modernized simulation options add separately identified variants rather than silently expanding F22-D claims. G8 closes only the advertised selected profile, with all exclusions explicit. Generic numeric budgets remain MOD-P under every profile.

Practical execution order: **M00 -> M01 -> M02 -> M05 basic envelope -> M03 -> M04 -> M06 -> M07 -> M08 -> M09 -> M10 -> M11 -> M12**. M05's extended envelope/thermal/tanker variants continue as their dependencies become available. Parallel engineering work can prepare fixtures/results, but no flight is gated by a test result from a different package.

Budget approximately **six hours for one nominal pass of the cards**, and **10-14 pilot/operator hours** for planned four-condition variants, resets and three-run deterministic spot repeats, excluding defect investigation and a full performance envelope. Split it into four sessions: (1) identity/ground/interface/NAV, (2) vehicle/AFCS/recovery, (3) A/A/EW and surface/weapon chains, (4) coupled faults/MP/VR/rehearsal. A 25-minute smoke selection may support iteration, but cannot substitute for this release campaign.

For a UI-only change, repeat its M02/M03/M08 interaction and the corresponding held-input/power-loss regression. For radar or target/weapon changes, repeat M06-M09 plus M11 donor/peer/source transitions. For EFM/power/fuel changes, repeat M01/M04/M05/M10 and M12. For a custom DLL, DCS native DLL/build, GPU renderer, EDM/material or input-package change, reopen M00 and all affected native/display/input gates; choose reruns from the actual dependency, not a blanket old green test suite.

Per-case record template: `run_id, case_id, package/mission hashes, baseline/options, setup/initial state, expected label and budget, prerequisites, exact pilot steps, actual values/timestamps, evidence paths, functional result, fidelity status, audit IDs, defect ID, reviewer, rerun linkage`. Store screenshots/video/CSV/event logs together under that run. Mission scoring is a summary of independently checked conditions, not the acceptance oracle; an aircraft script must not validate itself solely by reading its own success flag.

# F-22 overhaul: integration architecture, native feasibility and proof gates

Planning assignment B. Read-only review, 27 October 2026. This document proposes work; it does not change the aircraft, installed mod, canonical audit or any mission, and it does not report a new DCS test. No aircraft build or test suite was executed for this assignment. Existing test code was inspected. Source anchors below are relative to the immutable `overhaul/source/` text snapshot, not the live checkout.

Most physical utilities, cockpit transactions and degraded behavior can be implemented with owned C++/Lua state. Native radar, received radio messages, weapon internals and renderer callbacks use a materially more fragile integration tier.
